contractChanges.oldValue: Keep the book and its primary reading task dominant; use one quiet contextual connection control, a focused phone dialog with scan-first guidance and a direct return.
contractChanges.newValue: Keep the current passage legible and reachable, with operable contextual connection controls, focused QR/code guidance and direct return to the same Chronicle. Preserve an unobscured current heading and the existing substantive first-viewport reading-area and hit-test requirements. Editorial first-viewport dominance, utility grouping and appearance refinement are assigned to Project Refit; obstruction, unreadability and inaccessible controls remain Crossdeck blockers.

contractChanges.oldValue: Give each purpose its own full readable workspace beneath one Chronicle identity and connection status; make purpose change secondary and the return persistent, with camera-free meaningful Lens and actual map objectives.
contractChanges.newValue: Give each purpose its full readable workspace beneath one Chronicle identity and connection status, with discoverable, operable purpose selection and persistent unobscured return, camera-free meaningful Lens and actual map objectives. Editorial ranking and grouping of purpose/connection utilities and appearance refinement are assigned to Project Refit after all functional reading, purpose and return criteria pass.

contractChanges.oldValue: Keep the companion immersive, preserve compact account/context controls, and make the safe library exit and re-entry readable on desktop and phone.
contractChanges.newValue: Keep account/context controls and safe library exit and same-Voyage re-entry readable, discoverable and operable on desktop and phone in both motion modes. Relative passage/chrome composition after return and editorial appearance refinement are assigned to Project Refit; no functional, accessibility or continuity defect is deferred.

scopeAdjudication.requiredFunctionalScope: Essential readability and unchanged280x211 heading/hit-test/overflow, operable accessible controls, same-Voyage identity/edition/progression/return, actual purposes/Lens/maps/released content, privacy/security and truthful fallback; B2 and all other blockers remain fully resolvable requirements

composition.observation: The connection dialog sits over the journal rather than replacing it; after pairing, a narrow status strip appears above the book.

hierarchy.observation: The paired voyage title stays in view while the dialog's 'Bring your phone aboard' heading and QR code lead the immediate task.

typography.observation: The voyage uses a large serif title, but device status, expiry, and secondary link text are compact and can be hard to scan quickly.

spacing.observation: Desktop has room for a QR code and connection instructions; phone width turns the dialog into a long column with lower device details below the fold.

controls.observation: Connect another device, a code alternative, close, and continue are visibly separate, and paired captures expose send-to-phone and companion controls.

contrast.observation: The QR block and gold outlined close control are clear, while connection status and small device labels merge more with the dark shell.

consistency.observation: The connection dialog and returned journal retain common framing across normal and reduced motion and across desktop and phone.

states.observation: The dialog's ready and connected views differ, and the paired captures add pending, acknowledged, offline, reconnected, and revoked surfaces.

responsive.observation: On phone, the journal compresses into one column with bottom navigation; an additional landscape capture shows the companion can use a wider view.

keyboard.observation: Outlined connect and close controls appear in captures, but the recordings do not demonstrate a full keyboard path through pairing and transfer.

focus.observation: The ready dialog gives close a visible gold ring; later paired desktop captures keep the selected connection controls outlined.

feedback.observation: Pairing changes the dialog to a connected confirmation; transfer screens distinguish pending delivery from an acknowledged result.

motion.observation: The reduced connection run preserves the same readable journal and dialog states while the sampled normal run shows more book motion.

continuity.observation: After pairing, the journal remains at the active voyage and the companion names the same Voyage; reconnect and return states keep that identity visible.

complexity.observation: Connection, purpose selection, sending, receipt, offline handling, and return each have their own surface, adding many small decisions around the journal.

role-outcomes.observation: The desktop player can keep the Chronicle open while the phone serves as a same-Voyage companion, receives offers, and later returns to the Chronicle.

fallbacks.observation: The phone shows offline released content with Retry and later a reconnection status; adverse captures refuse an expired code and expose recovery after access ends.

findings.observation: The original major first-viewport and utility-hierarchy defect remains in history. Current reading, control, purpose, and return functions pass; remaining editorial composition is the exact approved Refit transfer.
findings.resolution: The contextual QR/code dialog, pairing, transfer receipts and same-Voyage return remain usable across desktop and phone in normal and reduced motion. The first phone Journal viewport and open desktop receipt have targeted geometry assertions in the current browser source. The compact status strip and utility ranking remain editorial Refit work.

functionalResolution.observation: Current same-contract screenshots and recorded transitions show readable active content, operable controls, intact same-Voyage route and return in the relevant phone contexts. Current browser geometry and accessibility assertions support the functional reading boundary.

findings.observation: The historical pending/acknowledged desktop receipt and restored phone Journal reading-area obstruction required complete resolution; no B2 deferral is authorized.
findings.resolution: Current normal and reduced desktop captures show full transfer receipt beside the open drawer, and phone return/continuation captures show the active Journal. The candidate browser source asserts receipt line visibility and first-viewport heading, hit-test, overflow and at least 280-by-211 reading-band geometry without scroll or hiding the surface.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: The contextual QR/code dialog, pairing, transfer receipts and same-Voyage return remain usable across desktop and phone in normal and reduced motion. The first phone Journal viewport and open desktop receipt have targeted geometry assertions in the current browser source. The compact status strip and utility ranking remain editorial Refit work.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: Device status, expiry and secondary links are small and subdued; the phone connection dialog is long. Sampled media alone did not prove full tab order or exact animation timing. Current journey accessibility assertions and source tests add bounded coverage, not a physical-user finding.

composition.observation: The companion purpose changes within the same shell from lens to chart to artifact and back to journal, with each purpose getting its own main card.

hierarchy.observation: 'Your companion' and purpose titles identify the phone's role; the Voyage name and Return to Chronicle remain above the changing content.

typography.observation: Serif passage and artifact titles make content distinct from sans-serif purpose controls, though helper copy around the chart is quite small.

spacing.observation: Desktop cards have breathing room; on phone, chart art and artifact reading occupy most of a long vertical screen and controls fall lower.

controls.observation: The lens has Choose/Inspect/Place controls, while chart and artifact have distinct content; Send to another screen and Change companion purpose remain available.

contrast.observation: Cream note, chart, and artifact cards read against dark teal; secondary sync and selector labels remain small and lower contrast.

consistency.observation: The Voyage identity, dark shell, gold focus treatments, and paper content treatment persist through purpose changes and reduced motion.

states.observation: Lens ready, chart ready, artifact ready, journal restored, and returned states each expose the current purpose or destination in visible text.

responsive.observation: The mobile cards fit a narrow viewport and keep Return to Chronicle visible, but the chart and artifact extend below one screen.

keyboard.observation: Visible outlines target the lens close and purpose headings, but the media does not establish keyboard traversal of the whole purpose selector.

focus.observation: Gold focus styling appears on the lens close and chart heading; the artifact and journal text-size controls have more subtle focus cues.

feedback.observation: The shell identifies 'Same Voyage · in sync', and restored journal content returns with the released passage and current chart context.

motion.observation: Normal and reduced recordings both cycle through purpose changes and return to the journal; reduced frames show a stable readable page during return.

continuity.observation: The restored journal and final returned Chronicle carry the same Voyage identity and objective after phone purpose changes.

complexity.observation: Four companion purposes plus offline/chart options create a dense phone flow; visible labels help, but the meaning of each purpose requires reading.

role-outcomes.observation: The player can inspect a clue, view the chart and released artifact, return to the journal companion, and resume the Chronicle.

fallbacks.observation: The reduced phone recording shows offline chart/device options and a same-device fallback message; the released card remains readable without live chart positioning.

findings.observation: The original major first-viewport and utility-hierarchy defect remains in history. Current reading, control, purpose, and return functions pass; remaining editorial composition is the exact approved Refit transfer.
findings.resolution: Released Lens clue, current Chart objective, artifact, restored Journal and return occupy distinct same-Voyage purpose workspaces. Current paired runs prove authorized delivery, acknowledgment, offline recovery and return; the source enforces crew/private separation. Purpose and connection utility ranking remains editorial Refit work.

functionalResolution.observation: Current same-contract screenshots and recorded transitions show readable active content, operable controls, intact same-Voyage route and return in the relevant phone contexts. Current browser geometry and accessibility assertions support the functional reading boundary.

findings.observation: The historical pending/acknowledged desktop receipt and restored phone Journal reading-area obstruction required complete resolution; no B2 deferral is authorized.
findings.resolution: Current normal and reduced desktop captures show full transfer receipt beside the open drawer, and phone return/continuation captures show the active Journal. The candidate browser source asserts receipt line visibility and first-viewport heading, hit-test, overflow and at least 280-by-211 reading-band geometry without scroll or hiding the surface.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: Released Lens clue, current Chart objective, artifact, restored Journal and return occupy distinct same-Voyage purpose workspaces. Current paired runs prove authorized delivery, acknowledgment, offline recovery and return; the source enforces crew/private separation. Purpose and connection utility ranking remains editorial Refit work.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: Phone chart and artifact content form a long page; helper and sync labels are small, and four purpose choices create scan cost. Sampled media did not establish complete keyboard traversal, while current journey assertions and source tests provide bounded browser coverage.

composition.observation: The Voyage Journal occupies the page behind a centered Chronicle Lens dialog; the parchment clue is visually isolated inside the darker dialog.

hierarchy.observation: The voyage title and active objective establish context before the lens title and Captain's note direct attention to one clue.

typography.observation: Large serif voyage and note headings contrast with compact sans-serif dialog guidance, while the clue itself uses readable dark text on parchment.

spacing.observation: The desktop clue has comfortable margins around its three actions; on mobile those actions wrap within the narrow card and consume more vertical space.

controls.observation: Choose, Inspect, Place in Guided View, close, and the returned Open Chronicle Lens control are distinct choices in the captured flow.

contrast.observation: The light note panel has strong text contrast; the subdued surrounding journal and tiny explanatory line under the note are less legible.

consistency.observation: Normal and reduced captures keep the same clue wording, action family, and modal treatment on desktop and phone.

states.observation: The inspected state adds an explicit interaction-recorded message and persists the note before the view returns to the journal.

responsive.observation: The modal fits a 390-pixel phone viewport and keeps the note readable, though it covers almost all of the journal behind it.

keyboard.observation: A gold outline is visible on the close control in the ready capture; the recording does not prove a complete keyboard path through all three note actions.

focus.observation: Focus emphasis is visible around close and later Open Chronicle Lens, making the immediate dialog exit and reopen actions identifiable.

feedback.observation: After Inspect, the modal says the interaction was recorded and invites continuation; the returned journal exposes the lens reopen action.

motion.observation: Normal recording frames show a turning journal before and after the modal; reduced frames keep a readable page-turn fallback with the same clue state.

continuity.observation: Closing the inspected clue returns to the same journal and objective, and the spatial moment remains available through Open Chronicle Lens.

complexity.observation: The single Captain's note has three verbs whose differences are not explained in depth on the card; the immediate Inspect feedback reduces some ambiguity.

role-outcomes.observation: The player can read and inspect a published clue without leaving the voyage; the note explicitly says this device uses Guided View.

fallbacks.observation: The reduced view states that page turning uses a readable fallback, and the clue itself remains accessible in the reduced recording.

findings.observation: The three verbs on the clue need reading to distinguish, and small guidance is less legible on phone. These are polish concerns within the witnessed browser path; Creator authoring, spatial camera behavior and Parallax acceptance remain outside this review.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: The released Captain's clue is readable in the Guided View dialog, Inspect produces explicit feedback, and closing returns to the same Journal in all four generic contexts.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: The three verbs on the clue need reading to distinguish, and small guidance is less legible on phone. These are polish concerns within the witnessed browser path; Creator authoring, spatial camera behavior and Parallax acceptance remain outside this review.

composition.observation: A single cream access card centers on a dark shell and changes from player entry to sign-in to password recovery.

hierarchy.observation: The large card heading leads each step; the player-account and invitation-code choice precedes the sign-in form and recovery link.

typography.observation: Large serif headings and dark card text are readable, while trusted-provider explanations and unavailable labels are considerably smaller.

spacing.observation: The centered desktop card has ample blank margin; phone width fits the card but pushes provider explanations down the page.

controls.observation: The entry card offers account and invitation choices, sign-in fields, and Forgot Password; recovery presents an email field and reset button.

contrast.observation: Black text and gold action buttons stand out on the cream card; small gray provider status text is less prominent.

consistency.observation: The same cream card, gold primary action, and Safe return affordance persist through normal and reduced captures on both device sizes.

states.observation: Entry, sign-in, and recovery are visibly separate states; provider buttons are presented as unavailable rather than apparently active.

responsive.observation: On mobile the access card stays within the viewport width, with form controls in one column and the return action retained in the header.

keyboard.observation: A visible outline surrounds the Sign in heading in one capture, but the recordings do not prove tab order or form submission behavior.

focus.observation: Gold outlining identifies the currently targeted heading or action in captured frames; the button gradient itself is not a focus substitute.

feedback.observation: The recovery view explicitly asks for email and labels its reset action; no sent-confirmation state appears in this packet.

motion.observation: Normal and reduced recordings both traverse entry, sign-in, recovery, and a return card; no necessary meaning depends on visible motion in sampled frames.

continuity.observation: Safe return remains in the header during account steps, and the recorded flow returns to the 'Bring the adventure with you' card.

complexity.observation: The entry step combines player account, invitation code, account creation, and recovery; provider explanations increase copy density below the form.

role-outcomes.observation: An anonymous visitor can reach account sign-in and password recovery and can return safely to the prior public surface.

fallbacks.observation: When Google or GitHub is unavailable, the sign-in card says so and directs use of email and password or return later.

findings.observation: Trusted-provider explanation text is small and the entry card combines several choices. The capture does not show a reset email sent or real OAuth completion, so those outcomes are not claimed.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: Anonymous player entry reaches sign-in and password recovery and returns safely on desktop and phone in both motion modes; unavailable providers are explicitly labeled and email entry stays operable.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: Trusted-provider explanation text is small and the entry card combines several choices. The capture does not show a reset email sent or real OAuth completion, so those outcomes are not claimed.

composition.observation: The desktop companion uses a narrow reading column; returning to the Chronicle Library reveals a wider catalog before the Voyage Journal fills the screen.

hierarchy.observation: Voyage identity and 'Journal companion' establish purpose, while 'Return to Chronicle' and later the active Voyage card direct the next action.

typography.observation: Serif passage and library headings distinguish reading material from small sans-serif controls and synchronization labels.

spacing.observation: The companion column has generous desktop side margins, though the card stacks selector, reading size, and passage vertically.

controls.observation: Return to Chronicle, released-passage selection, and reading-size controls are visible; the library then exposes search and gallery/list controls.

contrast.observation: Dark text on the cream passage card reads clearly; the surrounding dark shell uses much smaller subdued sync and utility labels.

consistency.observation: Companion, library, and journal keep the same Voyage identity, header treatment, and warm paper reading surface across reduced and normal captures.

states.observation: 'Same Voyage · in sync' appears on the companion, 'Server confirmed' on the library, and the returned journal shows an active objective.

responsive.observation: This desktop contract demonstrates a wide library and journal; the separate mobile contract contains the narrow-screen variant.

keyboard.observation: A gold outline appears on the library heading, but the recording does not establish keyboard traversal through search, filters, and return.

focus.observation: The outlined library heading gives a visible target; the companion's text-size controls have much subtler borders.

feedback.observation: Sync and server-confirmed labels give continuity feedback, while the returned journal again displays the current objective.

motion.observation: Sampled normal and reduced recordings both pass through the companion, library, and journal; reduced frames keep readable fallback pages.

continuity.observation: The voyage title persists from companion to library entry and back to the Chronicle; the recorded return does not reset the shown passage objective.

complexity.observation: Moving from a single reading companion to a searchable library and then the journal adds navigation steps, but each screen states the same Voyage context.

role-outcomes.observation: The player can read a released passage on the companion, return through the Chronicle Library, and resume the Voyage Journal.

fallbacks.observation: The reduced capture keeps page turning in a readable fallback after return; no separate error recovery is shown in this contract's screenshots.

findings.observation: Sync and utility labels remain compact, and the library adds navigation steps. This contract's capture does not exercise a failed return; its successful return and browser accessibility assertions are the supported scope.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: The desktop companion carries a released passage and same-Voyage status into the Chronicle Library and restored Journal in normal and reduced motion.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: Sync and utility labels remain compact, and the library adds navigation steps. This contract's capture does not exercise a failed return; its successful return and browser accessibility assertions are the supported scope.

composition.observation: The phone companion, library, and journal all use a single narrow content column with a persistent compact header.

hierarchy.observation: The companion names the Voyage and passage before Return to Chronicle; the library title and active Voyage section then guide the exit route.

typography.observation: The serif library heading and cream passage remain readable at phone width, while shell metadata and small navigation text are densely set.

spacing.observation: The phone stacks companion controls and passage, then stacks library search, filters, and results; the journal adds bottom tabs and an objective bar.

controls.observation: Return to Chronicle, released-passage select, reading size, library search/filter/view controls, and journal navigation are visibly labeled.

contrast.observation: The cream reading panel is legible on dark teal; lower-priority sync and navigation labels have weaker visual contrast and smaller size.

consistency.observation: Normal and reduced phone captures preserve the same card, header, Voyage name, and destination sequence.

states.observation: The phone capture shows a connecting check before library return, then 'Server confirmed' and a restored active journal page.

responsive.observation: The 390-pixel layout avoids horizontal overflow in sampled screenshots, though one viewport cannot show the full library form and result together.

keyboard.observation: The library heading has a visible outline in reduced phone capture, but no complete keyboard sequence is observable from this media.

focus.observation: Outline emphasis around the library heading survives the phone layout; the compact header controls remain separately bounded.

feedback.observation: Connecting, server-confirmed, and returned-journal text visibly mark the route back to the active Voyage.

motion.observation: Normal and reduced recordings show the same companion-to-library-to-journal sequence, with the reduced journal remaining readable as a still page.

continuity.observation: The Voyage identity persists on the phone companion and journal; return through the library restores the same active objective.

complexity.observation: The route has three surfaces and many small phone controls, but the repeated Return and Voyage labels help explain where the player is.

role-outcomes.observation: The phone player can leave a released reading companion, find the active Voyage in the library, and resume the journal.

fallbacks.observation: The connecting state and Safe Return-style route are visible in recording frames; this contract does not show a failed return or retry screen.

findings.observation: The original major first-viewport and utility-hierarchy defect remains in history. Current reading, control, purpose, and return functions pass; remaining editorial composition is the exact approved Refit transfer.
findings.resolution: At 390px, the companion, library and Journal remain a single-column same-Voyage route. The normal and reduced captures show an operable return and active objective; current paired flow also clicks Continue Voyage and sees completion. Relative passage/chrome composition remains editorial Refit work.

functionalResolution.observation: Current same-contract screenshots and recorded transitions show readable active content, operable controls, intact same-Voyage route and return in the relevant phone contexts. Current browser geometry and accessibility assertions support the functional reading boundary.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: At 390px, the companion, library and Journal remain a single-column same-Voyage route. The normal and reduced captures show an operable return and active objective; current paired flow also clicks Continue Voyage and sees completion. Relative passage/chrome composition remains editorial Refit work.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: Small header and navigation labels, a lengthy library form, and the objective bar make the first phone viewport dense. Sampled media cannot prove every keyboard step; current browser journey assertions and the dedicated first-viewport helper are bounded corroboration.

composition.observation: The desktop preparation screen divides the camera preview and setup copy; calibration turns that left area into a bounded pointing field.

hierarchy.observation: The large 'Find your point' title and four numbered steps establish a route from preparation to exploration, with the current stage accented.

typography.observation: Serif stage titles distinguish the interaction from the small sans-serif instructions; the diagnostics and privacy text are much smaller than the main prompt.

spacing.observation: Desktop gives the pointing field broad space, whereas the mobile flow becomes a long vertical sequence with controls and preview separated by scrolling.

controls.observation: The flow exposes camera and guided-demo starts, mode choice, pause, retry, cancel, and later playground actions as separately labeled controls.

contrast.observation: Gold primary actions and the pointing boundary stand out on dark teal, but muted status, progress, and diagnostic lines appear relatively faint.

consistency.observation: Absolute and relative exercises retain the same field, target marker, stage labels, and action styling while changing the movement instructions.

states.observation: Paused, independent-check-required, checking, passed, and ineligible states each show different wording or symbols rather than a silent surface change.

responsive.observation: At phone width the pointing field remains framed and the action buttons remain present, but only part of the long setup and results content fits at once.

keyboard.observation: Captured outlines around the title, action buttons, and select show visible keyboard-style targeting; the media does not establish full traversal order.

focus.observation: The highlighted target and gold control outline make the active area or control perceptible, although some faint secondary text remains easy to miss.

feedback.observation: Target count and percent progress, hand-readiness copy, check results, and camera-unavailable recovery text give state-specific feedback.

motion.observation: Recorded normal and reduced runs both advance from target collection to independent check; sampled frames support state continuity, not exact animation timing.

continuity.observation: The recorded exercise reaches a distinct 'Bring the adventure with you' return card after the local pointing sequence; no saved calibration is claimed on that card.

complexity.observation: Camera setup, two pointing modes, target training, an independent check, diagnostics, and playground options compete for attention in this single journey.

role-outcomes.observation: Anonymous users can complete the guided demo and independent check and reach the playground; the later card offers sign-in to connect screens.

fallbacks.observation: When camera start fails, the screen names the problem and offers 'Retry live camera' and 'Explore guided demo' rather than ending the flow.

findings.observation: The long phone setup, muted diagnostics and camera terminology demand sustained reading. Guided synthetic success does not qualify real-person pointing accuracy, physical hardware, screen-reader use, or owner acceptance; absolute empirical pointing remains experimental.

reviews.sourceQualifiedJudgment: The guided demonstration moves through absolute and relative training, held-out validation, results, playground, ineligible hand states, camera failure recovery and safe return. Current browser tests also cover keyboard targets, worker lifecycle and aggregate export consent.
reviews.contraryObservationsAndGaps: The long phone setup, muted diagnostics and camera terminology demand sustained reading. Guided synthetic success does not qualify real-person pointing accuracy, physical hardware, screen-reader use, or owner acceptance; absolute empirical pointing remains experimental.
